title: TinyAlign: Boosting Lightweight Vision-Language Models by Mitigating Modal Alignment Bottlenecks

items.abstract: <jats:p>Vision-language models such as CLIP have shown impressive zero-shot recognition performance by aligning images and text in a shared embedding space. However, their generalization often deteriorates in few-shot settings due to the inflexibility of handcrafted textual templates and limited adaptability to novel visual domains. To overcome these limitations, we propose HiCKP, a hierarchical cross-modal prompt learning framework that enables deep, structured alignment between visual and textual prompts across multiple transformer layers. HiCKP introduces stage-wise proxy tokens to capture layer-specific semantic cues and refines prompts through a cross-modal adaptive gated konwledge module that dynamically balances modality interactions. Furthermore, we incorporate external semantic knowledge from large language models during training, using rich natural language descriptions to regularize textual prompts via  alignment objectives. This LLM-guided supervision significantly improves semantic discrimination, especially for fine-grained or visually similar categories. Extensive experiments across eleven diverse datasets demonstrate that HiCKP achieves better performance in base-to-novel generalization, consistently surpassing existing prompt-based and adapter-based approaches under various few-shot configurations. Ablation studies validate the individual contributions of hierarchical prompting, cross-modal coordination, and LLM-informed regularization to the overall effectiveness of our method.</jats:p>
title: Hierarchical Cross-Modal Prompt Learning with LLM-Guided Alignment for Vision-Language Models

items.abstract: Vision-language models possess cross-modal generalization capabilities in zero-shot image classification. Existing methods improve classification accuracy by generating fine-grained text descriptions via large language models and aligning them with local image region features. However, these approaches suffer from two limitations: (1) random or semi-random cropping tends to introduce background noise and lose discriminative details, while failing to adaptively adjust the observation scale based on region-wise semantic importance; (2) there exists a many-to-many matching relationship between local regions and text descriptions, yet current methods adopt one-way independent weight computation and do not explicitly model the bidirectional correlation between regions and descriptions. To address these issues, this paper proposes attention-guided local dynamic alignment (ALDA), which achieves cross-modal fine-grained semantic alignment without training or fine-tuning. We reveal and model two core dynamic properties: spatial sampling dynamics, where the location and scale of discriminative regions vary with image content, and semantic matching dynamics, where region weights and description weights mutually define and co-evolve. ALDA employs attention-driven adaptive multi-scale sampling to locate discriminative regions and allocate observation scales, reducing background noise and focusing on details. It further performs bidirectional iterative propagation on a region-description bipartite graph to achieve mutual reinforcement of weights and matching convergence. Experimental results on six standard datasets and four out-of-distribution generalization benchmarks show that ALDA achieves an average accuracy of 69.17% on the ViT-B/16 backbone, with consistent performance improvements in fine-grained classification and natural adversarial scenarios, while maintaining inference efficiency and interpretability.
title: Attention-guided local dynamic alignment: Boosting zero-shot classification of vision-language models
